sections.label: THINKING
sections.content:
Interesting! When I pressed LEFT with the avatar aligned to the red block:
- The track went from 2 blocks to 0 blocks (retracted by 2)
- But the red block didn't move! It stayed at cols 42-45
- The blue block also stayed at cols 24-27
So LEFT only moves the colored block that's on the same row as the avatar AND is connected to the track. When the avatar is at rows 18-23 (aligned with red), the track is at rows 18-23, and the red block is at rows 19-22. But the track only extends to col 22, and the red block is at col 42-45. So the track doesn't reach the red block!
Wait, but when the avatar was at rows 30-35 (aligned with blue), the track was at rows 30-35, and the blue block was at rows 31-34. The track extended to col 22 (or more), and the blue block was at col 24-27 (or further). So the track reached the blue block!
The key insight is: the track extends from the avatar to the right, and it needs to reach the colored block for LEFT/RIGHT to move that block. When the track is too short, LEFT/RIGHT only changes the track length without moving the block.
So when the avatar is at rows 18-23 and the track is at 0 blocks, the track doesn't reach the red block (which is at cols 42-45). I need to extend the track (RIGHT) until it reaches the red block, then LEFT will move the red block.
Let me try RIGHT multiple times to extend the track until it reaches the red block.
Actually wait, let me reconsider. When the avatar was at rows 30-35 and the track was at 2 blocks (cols 17-22), the blue block was at cols 24-27. The track ended at col 22, and the blue block started at col 24. There was a 1-column gap. But LEFT still moved the blue block!
So the track doesn't need to physically touch the block for LEFT/RIGHT to work. The "active" block is simply the one on the same row as the avatar.
But then why didn't the red block move when I pressed LEFT with the avatar at rows 18-23?
Let me think... Maybe the track needs to be at least 2 blocks for LEFT/RIGHT to move the block. When I pressed LEFT, the track went from 2 to 0, and the red block didn't move. Maybe the rule is: LEFT/RIGHT only moves the block if the track is at least 2 blocks.
Or maybe the rule is different: LEFT/RIGHT moves the block only if the track was already extended enough to "grab" the block. When the avatar first aligns with a new block, the track needs to be extended (RIGHT) to grab it, then LEFT can pull it.
Let me try RIGHT to extend the track and see if the red block moves.

sections.label: TOOL CALL: python
sections.content:
<tool_call>
<function=python>
<parameter=code>
# LEFT with avatar at red block: track went 2->0, but red didn't move!
# Maybe the track needs to be extended to "grab" the block first
# Let me try RIGHT to extend the track and see if red moves

result = action(['RIGHT'])
print("Result - gameplay_changed:", last_action_result.get('gameplay_changed'))

seg = current_frame.segmentation['nodes']

# Check colored blocks
for n in seg:
    if n['color'] in ['R', 'b', 'N'] and n['pixels'] == 16 and min(p[0] for p in n['boundary']) < 50:
        b = n['boundary']
        minr = min(p[0] for p in b)
        maxr = max(p[0] for p in b)
        minc = min(p[1] for p in b)
        maxc = max(p[1] for p in b)
        print("Colored %s: rows %d-%d, cols %d-%d" % (n['color'], minr, maxr, minc, maxc))

# Check track
w_count = sum(1 for n in seg if n['color'] == 'w' and n['pixels'] == 4)
print("White blocks:", w_count)
</parameter>
</function>
</tool_call>
